question: Should OpenClaw adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus root-level inheritance as the supported long-term Microsoft Teams multi-account contract?
rationale: This adds compatibility-sensitive configuration, credential routing, setup behavior, and persisted-state namespaces across the entire Teams plugin; tests can validate mechanics, but they cannot decide whether the hybrid public contract and upgrade burden are acceptable.

options.title: Sponsor after repair
options.body: Approve the account model after the global turn-chain defect is fixed and live legacy-upgrade proof confirms root configuration and existing state remain usable.

options.title: Require one canonical shape
options.body: Require a doctor migration into `accounts` and remove steady-state hybrid runtime behavior before accepting the feature.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical feature request open but close or defer this branch if maintainers do not want to own the expanded Teams configuration and state contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repair
recommendation.body: Approve the account model after the global turn-chain defect is fixed and live legacy-upgrade proof confirms root configuration and existing state remain usable.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest available routing signal across adjacent Microsoft Teams lifecycle work and prior review context.
